## Context

A 40-minute full suite intermittently classifies the shared dribbling fake remote as stalled. The unchanged test passes in isolation. The helper sends rate // 10 bytes per nominal 0.1-second wake-up, so delayed wake-ups reduce cumulative throughput. A cumulative catch-up fix removes that drift, but a full-suite experiment still produced one uninterrupted gap long enough to trip the artificial 2-second window. Production intentionally uses a 10-second window and must not change.

## Proven root cause

The tests apply the same artificial 2-second window to zero-byte positive controls and above-floor negative controls. Libcurl correctly aborts any sufficiently long no-byte interval, so a scheduler-delayed Python fixture cannot make the negative control deterministic. Runtime experiments showed a 4-second pause trips a 2-second window, a 2.5-second pause does not trip a 10-second window, and a 10.5-second pause trips the 10-second window.

## Plan

1. Extract the helper's cumulative bytes-owed calculation and prove delayed wake-up catch-up with a pure deterministic unit test.
2. Keep the 2-second window only for zero-byte stall tests at every wrapper surface.
3. Keep one real Git/libcurl above-floor negative control at the shared snapshot boundary, using the production 10-second window and a transfer long enough to cross it.
4. Remove redundant live dribble timing trials at wrapper call sites; their existing argv tests already prove each wrapper installs the shared low-speed configuration.
5. Run both consumer modules and the full suite. Verify src/rebar/_snapshot/git_fetch.py has no diff.

This follows the common layered-test pattern: deterministic mechanism coverage, one integration contract at the shared boundary, and per-caller wiring tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A pure test proves cumulative bytes owed equals floor(rate * elapsed) minus bytes already sent after a delayed wake-up.
- [x] Every zero-byte stall case still fails specifically as a stall under the fast 2-second test window.
- [x] One real Git above-floor transfer remains a non-stall failure across the production 10-second window.
- [x] Deterministic argv tests prove every wrapper still installs the shared low-speed options.
- [x] git diff origin/main -- src/rebar/_snapshot/git_fetch.py is empty and the full default suite passes.

## Evidence

The original full suite passed 11,881 tests before one dribble failure. The cumulative-only attempt passed 13 focused tests but a second full suite passed 11,852 tests before another dribble failure, proving catch-up alone is insufficient.
